subject: Request: Temporary p50/p95 grace & evidence handoff for Hosted API
messages:
From: Gregory Shaw <greg.shaw@finpay.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO exception & grace request for upcoming migration

Laura —

Quick note from our infra team: FinPay is doing a payment gateway migration on Oct 2 that will change traffic patterns for a 72-hour window. We expect spikes as the new gateway warms up and a small percentage of requests will hit long tail backends for reconciliation (estimated ~2% of requests).

To avoid a premature breach while we validate the cutover, can Redwood provide a temporary grace on the hosted API p95 for that 72 hour window (we're asking for a +20% relative buffer to the contract p95)? We also need the SLO evidence pack and any mutual action plan you use for these migration carveouts — procurement needs that to sign off.

Specifically FinPay asks:
- A written exception that covers Oct 2 00:00 UTC through Oct 4 23:59 UTC
- Clarify what measurement window you will use (rolling minute vs hourly buckets) during the exception
- A list of observability artifacts you will provide (traces, token-level latency breakdown, sample requests)

Can you confirm what you need from us (sample traffic, cutover schedule, contact for on-call)?

Thanks,
Greg Shaw
Head of Platform Ops, FinPay
greg.shaw@finpay.com

Greg —

Thanks for the heads-up and the clear ask. We can support a temporary, documented grace for the hosted API p95 during your migration window. To keep operations tight and auditable we'd like to lock the following:

Our proposal (summary):
- Exception window: 2026-10-02T00:00:00Z through 2026-10-04T23:59:59Z (UTC)
- Operational carveout: Allow up to +20% relative on the contracted p95 for the window; p50 remains unchanged
- Measurement approach during the carveout: rolling 5-minute quantile windows for alerting, 1-hour aggregated epochs for contractual evidence (we'll show both)
- Evidence we will provide: token-level latency distribution, representative traces, sampling of 1,000 request IDs across the window, and the SLO evidence pack (zipped).

What we need from FinPay to finalize:
1) Confirm cutover start/end timestamps (UTC) and an on-call contact for the migration (name + mobile).
2) Provide a sample of the expected traffic distribution (percent of traffic hitting reconciliation backend) or let us run a short 15-min canary before T0.
3) Sign the mutual action plan (I attached an editable MAP: mutual-action-plan.xlsx).

Operational notes:
- We'll apply the exception to the Hosted API model route(s) you use and pin the rollout to avoid auto-quantization changes during the window.
- During the window we'll enable extra tracing and increase our token-level retention for FinPay traces by 72 hours to support post-mortem.

Next steps:
- If you confirm the timestamps and the MAP, I'll loop in Aditya (runtime) and Ben (customer success) and we'll prepare the SLO evidence pack ahead of T0.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: aditya.rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed measurement & mitigation for FinPay migration (notes)

Team —

Notes to operationalize Laura's reply. I want to capture this here before we send the formal exception doc:

Technical proposal (detailed):
- Baseline contract SLOs: p50 = 60 ms, p95 = 280 ms (hosted-route: finpay-payments-v2).
- Temporary allowance: p95 allowance = +20% relative => contract p95 * 1.20 = 336 ms. We'll record both the absolute and relative metrics in the evidence pack.
- Measurement windows:
  * Real-time alerting: rolling 5-minute quantile (helps on-call catch regressions quickly).
  * Contract evidence: 1-hour aggregation buckets (aligned to UTC epoch boundaries) and a post-window 24-hour summary.
  * Rationale: 5-minute rolling gives sensitivity for operational mitigation; 1-hour aggregation is less sensitive to momentary microbursts but still granular for audit.
- Canary plan: recommend FinPay run a 15-minute canary at ~10% traffic three hours before full cutover. If p95 breaches > +15% during canary, hold and triage.
- Sampling / artifacts we will include in slo-evidence-pack.zip: token-latency-cdf.csv, trace-samples.jsonl (1k items), route-cost-breakdown.tsv, canary-report.pdf.

Risk controls / guardrails:
- We'll implement an automatic fallback to the stable model variant if p95 > +40% sustained for 10 minutes during the window. That prevents broader customer impact.
- Any fallback will be logged and included in the final post-mortem.

Operational ask of FinPay:
- One primary on-call (name + mobile) during the window for rapid coordination.
- A DocuSign approval on the mutual action plan (we'll provide link once MAP is finalized).

I'll assemble the exception letter and evidence pack once Laura confirms we can proceed. Ben, can you coordinate the DocuSign and CS playbook? Marissa, can you pre-generate the sample trace set and the token-latency csv?

-Aditya
